title: Redwood November 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company-wide all-hands. Updates on product, reliability, Q4 goals, hiring, and upcoming private deployment launches. Brief Q&A and shoutouts. Deck link shared in chat: https://redwood.company/allhands/2026-11-deck
topics: Product updates: Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize
action_items: Marcus Lee: Publish updated latency dashboard and post in #observability by 2026-12-07
Emily Chen: Share rollout plan for the new caching profile recommendations with PS and SE teams by 2026-12-03
Priya Nair: Send summary of top 5 enterprise contracts and upcoming renewals to GTM by 2026-12-01
Lena Ortiz: Finalize interview loop changes and update Hiring Handbook by 2026-12-10
next_steps: All-hands deck shared in chat (link above)
Team leads to run quarterly OKR reviews next week
Schedule follow-up reliability deep dive with infra (Marcus + Eng leads)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Rao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Sorry for a slight delay, we were setting up the slides. Um, welcome to the November all-hands. we've got a packed agenda, try to keep to an hour and then do Q&A.
[00:20] Emily Chen: Quick agenda, product updates, reliability, GTM, hiring and then Q&A. slide deck is in the chat, folks.
[00:35] Marcus Lee: I'll start with infra, tl;dr — latency is down 12% month over month, but we had two notable incidents in mid-Nov that cost about 45 minutes of elevated errors, root cause tracked to a kernel regression in a 3rd-party lib. we're rolling a hotfix and a postmortem is in the wiki.
[01:05] Priya Nair: On the GTM side we closed three key logos this month, two in fintech and one in healthcare. bookings look healthy for Q4, pipeline is up 28% vs last quarter.
[01:30] Samir Rao: Nice. Quick reminder on our thesis — serving is the moat. everything we do should make inference predictable and economical.
[01:45] Emily Chen: Product highlights: Redwood Dedicated — GA for reserved capacity in eu-west last week, early customers reporting stable per-token costs and much better tail latency. Redwood Private — pilot with a regulated healthcare customer moving to on-prem next month. Console — added token-level cost breakdowns and new routing policy UI. Optimize — rolling out first version of quantization recommendations for customer workloads.
[02:20] Speaker 1: Can you repeat the Dedicated region roll out? I think I missed the region name.
[02:25] Marcus Lee: yeah eu-west, and we're doing a staggered roll out in ap-southeast by Jan. note, some perf profile differences on older A100s vs newer H100s, the kernel selection heuristics need the new benchmark numbers.
[02:50] Samir Rao: On reliability, Marcus, can you summarize the incident and the action items?
[02:57] Marcus Lee: Sure — cause: upstream kernel regression in the vectorized attention lib. mitigation: rollback patch, apply test coverage to catch in canaries, add an additional perf regression test to CI. action items are on the postmortem doc. we'll also add an automated alert for kv-cache evictions which masked the issue.
[03:30] Emily Chen: On product roadmaps — we're prioritizing three things for Q1: 1) expand smart routing policies so customers can set cost vs latency SLOs, 2) improve cache sharing across multitenant workloads, 3) better private deployment UX — fewer manual network steps for VPCs.
[04:00] Speaker 2: Is the private on-prem package going to support HSM integration out of the box?
[04:10] Marcus Lee: short answer yes, we're shipping KMS/HSM integrations but enterprise setup requires a small ops runbook; aim is to reduce that friction.
[04:25] Priya Nair: From the sales front, entry motions are working — PLG funnel converting to POC quite well. main bottleneck is security review cycle for regulated customers. Tech team: we need to shorten the SSO/SAML and audit logs turnaround.
[04:50] Samir Rao: On security/compliance — we're on track for next SOC 2 renewal, iso scope expanded to cover private deployments. security docs were updated last week, link's in the chat.
[05:10] Emily Chen: Also quick product note — streaming improvements landed for the API, customers will see faster first token latencies for long prompts. it's shipping as beta to hosted customers first.
[05:30] Speaker 3: there was a question in chat about pricing for Dedicated — Priya, want to cover that?
[05:36] Priya Nair: Sure — committed reserved pools start with monthly SKUs and annual offers for discounts. we're also piloting burst capacity options for customers who need short spikes. follow up to share the pricing sheet.
[06:00] Samir Rao: Hiring update — we're at ~150 headcount, hiring across infra, product, sales. Lena, any notes?
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: yes, we revised interview loops to be faster, introduced candidate NPS survey, target is to cut time-to-offer by 20% next quarter. also internal mobility program launching in January.
[06:30] Speaker 4: Any notable customer stories this month?
[06:35] Priya Nair: A fintech customer moved from a competitor due to better tail latency and more predictable costs — they cited our telemetry and cost breakdown as a big win. healthcare pilot appreciated private deployment + audit logs.
[07:00] Marcus Lee: On engineering priorities — next sprint we'll focus on kernel selection improvements, better CI perf tests, and a small refactor to the batching layer to reduce latency variance.
[07:20] Emily Chen: Product experiments — we're A/B testing default cache TTLs and a new auto-batching suggestion surface in Console. initial numbers show 8-12% cost savings for chat-heavy workloads.
[07:45] Speaker 5: Are we sharing the evals we run with customers? I remember some requests.
[07:51] Emily Chen: Yes, we share curated eval sets and regression alerts; customers in pilot see the eval dashboard. need to make it more self-serve.
[08:05] Samir Rao: Quick finance note — burn is within plan but we need to be mindful of hiring cadence in H1. revenue comps are fine, but we have to hit key enterprise contracts in Q1.
[08:25] Speaker 6: question about price elasticity — do we have updated guidance?
[08:30] Priya Nair: pricing team is finishing the sensitivity model, will share with leadership this week.
[08:40] Marcus Lee: technical deep dive scheduled next Tuesday for anyone interested: topics will be kv-cache behavior, batching heuristics, and quantized kernel perf — invite coming.
[09:00] Samir Rao: Shoutouts — engineering on the Dedicated eu-west launch, support on onboarding the healthcare pilot, and ops for keeping infra rock solid through the incident. small applause.
[09:20] Speaker 7: quick nit — the transcript sometimes shows Speaker 1 etc, not exact names; that's the fireflies auto-attrib.
[09:30] Emily Chen: Ok let's open to Q&A, put Qs in chat or raise hand.
[10:10] Speaker 8: Sorry to jump, are we planning any new partnerships for APAC channel?
[10:20] Priya Nair: yes we're targeting two channel partners and a cloud marketplace listing in early 2027.
[10:40] Speaker 9: any change to enterprise support SLAs?
[10:45] Samir Rao: No change to core SLAs; enterprise add-on for faster SRE response is being formalized. we'll share tiers.
[11:00] Speaker 10: Will there be a follow-up on the incident postmortem?
[11:05] Marcus Lee: yes, postmortem and action items are in the wiki and I'll run a deep-dive with eng leads next week.
[11:25] Emily Chen: Closing notes — deck is in chat, lead managers please run OKR reviews, and team leads post hiring needs.
[11:45] Samir Rao: Thanks everyone. next all-hands is end of December, same time. we'll keep it to an hour.
[11:55] [meeting ends]
